text: First, let me set up the industrial CO2 laser cutter that was installed by our technicians last month in the main fabrication workshop. The protective enclosure with reinforced acrylic panels must be checked out before we turn on the high-powered 150-watt laser system. Sarah and Mike are putting together the safety protocols while I hook up the ventilation system that removes toxic fumes at 400 cubic feet per minute. The calibration procedure which was developed by our senior engineer requires us to heat up the laser tube to exactly 180 degrees Celsius over a 3-minute warm-up period. Next, the cutting bed is adjusted by the operator using precision micrometer controls to achieve a focal distance of 2.5 millimeters from the material surface. After that, we need to fire up the exhaust fan and turn on the air assist system before any cutting begins. The 6-millimeter birch plywood sheets that Sarah prepared earlier are positioned on the workbench while Mike sets up the computer-controlled cutting pattern. The emergency stop button which is located next to the control panel was tested by both operators at 2 PM today. Then, the laser power is ramped up gradually from 20 percent to full power over 30 seconds while the material feeds through at exactly 15 millimeters per second. Throughout this process, both Sarah and Mike monitor the cutting temperature and check for any flare-ups using the built-in camera system.
